title: Grateful Dead Live at P.N.E. Garden Auditorium on 1966-07-29

ai_review.summary: Excellent sound‑board capture of a scorching 1966 Vancouver set, highlighted by Cardboard Cowboy, Viola Lee Blues and Baby Blue with crisp organ and Jerry’s soaring guitar.
ai_review.review: The recording delivers surprisingly clear, almost studio‑quality sound for a mid‑60s tape, letting the band’s early psychedelic fire shine through. Standout moments include the monster “Cardboard Cowboy”, blistering “Viola Lee Blues”, and a jazzy “Baby Blue” where Jerry’s tone is described as perfect. Pigpen’s organ drives the jam‑heavy set and the overall performance is repeatedly called hot, experimental and one of the best early shows.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of detailed reviews award 4–5 stars, praising both performance and audio fidelity; average rating ≈4.65 leads to a strong overall score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp and clear for a 1966 tape, slight hiss/fuzziness noted but not detrimental; organ and guitars come through strongly, audience barely audible.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑mid‑60s set flows tightly with high‑energy renditions and extended jams; the band moves quickly through songs, delivering a raw yet cohesive psychedelic experience.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Tone on “Next Time You See Me” and “Baby Blue” called perfect; his guitar work described as ripping and central to the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Praised for high‑part harmonies on “Viola Lee Blues”; noted in historical context of the era’s vocal arrangements.
band_member_comments.Bob: Mentioned as low in the mix but still audible; no major criticism.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ highlighted throughout – especially on “Stealin’”, “Cream Puff War” and overall early psychedelic sound.
